name: Minimalist Product Motion Design
visualIdentity: Explicit: a normalized, descriptive presentation direction drawn from product-brand references, not a historical movement. It frames one product and a few meaningful details with generous space, concise copy, precise proportions, and restrained materials and light. It uses smooth close-ups and selective reveals with deliberate settling. Product accuracy is preserved, and campaign shots are not copied.
suitableUses: Explicit good fits: editorial narratives, product explainers, document, evidence, or process sequences, and flat vector, collage, sticker, or motion-poster layouts. Explicit hybrid examples: hero reveals, premium product launches, spec callouts, and closing taglines. Other uses are unspecified.
limitations: Explicit: adapt or omit when the stack hides content the viewer must read, when overlap obscures provenance, ordering, or comparison labels, or when fixed print geometry cannot accommodate stacking. Product accuracy and exact supplied colors take priority over style adaptation. The style is usually best used alone, since restraint is the point.
palette: Reference-dependent example applying only to new presentation elements. Tokens: background #F6F2EA and foreground #2A3030, used as discrete colors with no gradient. Foreground on background measures 12.026:1, meeting the 4.5:1 normal-text target. Task, brand, or product colors override these and are never recolored. The two-color check does not cover text over images or video, so composited frames must be rechecked.
motionAndInteraction: Explicit: smooth close-ups, selective reveals, and deliberate settling, with animation limited to purposeful details and camera moves. Shared guidance favors coherent easing but keeps deliberate cuts and reading holds, and adds no automatic spring or bounce. Video is driven by seekable composition time. Hover, scroll, and pointer behavior apply only to optional interactive delivery. Catalog motion references are optional and must be screened for fit.
audio: Not specified by the style; audio is a topic-based suggestion. Options include background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence, with no fixed genre, tempo, instrument, or voice. Inferred: restrained or silent audio may suit the reading holds, though the source does not state this. Speech must remain intelligible and unclipped.
assetRequirements: Not specified in the source; no required asset list is given. Inferred: the style needs product imagery or renders, detail views, and crisp interface layers. Genuine 3D products may need Blender prerenders. Photographs may need Cropper.js framing. Fonts and assets must load before rendering, and source artwork and product colors remain unchanged.
combinations: Usually best used alone. Optional hybrid with style-104 for axial, frontal push-ins on hero shots, using only the two tokens and no added props. Optional hybrid with style-093 for one short spec line at a time, not overlapping the product silhouette. Camera dolly and exploded-reveal patterns are listed as compatible but are not mandatory. Avoid pastel set dressing and expressive scale or spring motion on text.
productionApproach: Style renderer: Blender for genuine 3D product prerenders when needed, and SVG or native DOM for crisp interface elements. Motion engine: GSAP on a paused, seekable timeline, with Motion or Anime.js optional and only one owner per animated property. Render pipeline: HyperFrames is primary, and Remotion is used only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, with the reason recorded. Validate direct seeks, decoded frames, legibility, audio sync, and product accuracy.
